Explanation of the words:

"And He has created you in stages" (wa-qad khalaqakum atwaran): i.e., state after state: at times a drop of semen, at times a clinging clot, at times a lump of flesh.

"And made the sun a lamp" (wa-ja'al al-shamsa siraja): i.e., shining.

"And caused you to grow from the earth as a growth" (anbatakum min al-ard nabatan): i.e., He brought you into being from the dust of the earth.

"Then He will return you into it" (thumma yu'iduकum fiha): i.e., you will be buried in it.

"And will bring you out of it, a bringing forth" (wa-yukhrijukum minha ikhraja): i.e., on the Day of Resurrection.

"Broad roads" (subulan fijajan): i.e., wide paths.

The meanings of the verses:

These verses contain a radiant picture by whose light the guides and callers to God, may He be exalted, are guided. It represents an account of the situation which Noah presented to his Lord, the essence of a call that lasted nearly nine hundred and fifty years. Let us listen to Noah, peace be upon him, as he complains to his Lord and presents to Him what he has done in calling to Him. He said: ﴿My Lord, I have called my people﴾, who at that time were all the people of the earth, ﴿night and day﴾, i.e., by night and by day, since some people can only be reached at night. ﴿But my calling only increased them﴾ in turning away from faith in You and worshipping You alone ﴿in flight﴾ from me and from what I called them to. Whenever I called them so that You would forgive them, by their seeking Your forgiveness and turning to You, that You would forgive them, ﴿they put their fingers in their ears﴾ so that they would not hear what I say to them, ﴿and covered themselves with their garments﴾, i.e., wrapped themselves in them so that they would not see me or look at my face, out of hatred and dislike for me, ﴿and persisted﴾ in polytheism and disbelief with increasing persistence, out of obstinacy, ﴿and grew arrogant with an astonishing arrogance﴾.

﴿Then indeed I called them﴾ to affirm Your oneness in worship and to abandon association in it, ﴿openly﴾, i.e., publicly declaring that. ﴿Then indeed I announced to them and I confided to them in private, a private confiding﴾, according to the groups and circumstances. I knocked on every door seeking their response to the call and their acceptance of guidance, and I said: ﴿Seek forgiveness from your Lord; indeed He is ever Forgiving. He will send the sky upon you in abundant rain﴾, i.e., rain will fall upon you in succession, so there will be no drought or barrenness. ﴿And He will increase you in wealth and children﴾ as you desire. ﴿And He will make for you gardens﴾ of palm trees and grapevines, ﴿and He will make for you rivers﴾ flowing through those gardens, irrigating them. Then he turned to them and said, rebuking them for their recklessness and lack of fear: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not hope for dignity from God?﴾, i.e., what has befallen you, what has caused you not to hope for dignity from God, not to fear His greatness, power and majesty? ﴿And He has created you in stages﴾. He drew their attention to the manifestations of God's power, saying to them: ﴿Have you not seen how God created seven heavens in layers?﴾, one heaven above another, fitting one another. ﴿And made the moon therein a light﴾ illuminating what is above it of the heavens and what is below it of the earth. ﴿And made the sun a lamp﴾, blazing and shining, lighting the heavens with its face and the earth with its back, like the moon. ﴿And God caused you to grow from the earth as a growth﴾, since He made your origin from dust, and the drops of semen are also nourishment formed from the dust; then He created you resembling plants, following their pattern in life and growth.

﴿Then He will return you into it﴾, i.e., into the earth after death, so you are buried in it, ﴿and will bring you out of it﴾ also, ﴿a bringing forth﴾ on the Day of Resurrection for reckoning and recompense. ﴿And God made the earth for you a spread carpet﴾, i.e., laid out, spread flat, suitable for living upon and for life on it, ﴿that you may follow therein roads, broad paths﴾, i.e., wide ways. Thus Noah, peace be upon him, led them through the displays of God's cosmic signs, all of which indicate the existence of God, His power, knowledge, wisdom and mercy, and which necessitate worship of Him by reason, and the negation of it toward anything else. This was the problem of Noah and his account of his situation to his Lord, who knows it best. In this there is a great lesson for the guiding callers who are rightly guided, may God make us among them. Amen.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Laying out the correct path of calling, based on patience and varying the method.

2- Explanation of the disbelievers' aversion to monotheism and to the monotheists: because of their hatred of Noah and the call to monotheism, they stopped their ears so as not to hear, covered their faces so as not to see him, and grew arrogant so as not to regard him as having any merit.

Let us listen to Noah, peace be upon him, as he complains to his Lord and presents to Him what he has done in calling to Him. He said: ﴿My Lord, I have called my people﴾, who at that time were all the people of the earth, ﴿night and day﴾, i.e., by night and by day, since some people can only be reached at night. ﴿But my calling only increased them﴾ in turning away from faith in You and worshipping You alone ﴿in flight﴾ from me and from what I called them to. Whenever I called them so that You would forgive them, by their seeking Your forgiveness and turning to You, that You would forgive them, ﴿they put their fingers in their ears﴾ so that they would not hear what I say to them, ﴿and covered themselves with their garments﴾, i.e., wrapped themselves in them so that they would not see me or look at my face, out of hatred and dislike for me, ﴿and persisted﴾ in polytheism and disbelief with increasing persistence, out of obstinacy, ﴿and grew arrogant with an astonishing arrogance﴾.

﴿Then indeed I called them﴾ to affirm Your oneness in worship and to abandon association in it, ﴿openly﴾, i.e., publicly declaring that. ﴿Then indeed I announced to them and I confided to them in private, a private confiding﴾, according to the groups and circumstances. I knocked on every door seeking their response to the call and their acceptance of guidance, and I said: ﴿Seek forgiveness from your Lord; indeed He is ever Forgiving. He will send the sky upon you in abundant rain﴾, i.e., rain will fall upon you in succession, so there will be no drought or barrenness. ﴿And He will increase you in wealth and children﴾ as you desire. ﴿And He will make for you gardens﴾ of palm trees and grapevines, ﴿and He will make for you rivers﴾ flowing through those gardens, irrigating them. Then he turned to them and said, rebuking them for their recklessness and lack of fear: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not hope for dignity from God?﴾, i.e., what has befallen you, what has caused you not to hope for dignity from God, not to fear His greatness, power and majesty? ﴿And He has created you in stages﴾. He drew their attention to the manifestations of God's power, saying to them: ﴿Have you not seen how God created seven heavens in layers?﴾, one heaven above another, fitting one another. ﴿And made the moon therein a light﴾ illuminating what is above it of the heavens and what is below it of the earth. ﴿And made the sun a lamp﴾, blazing and shining, lighting the heavens with its face and the earth with its back, like the moon. ﴿And God caused you to grow from the earth as a growth﴾, since He made your origin from dust, and the drops of semen are also nourishment formed from the dust; then He created you resembling plants, following their pattern in life and growth.

﴿Then He will return you into it﴾, i.e., into the earth after death, so you are buried in it, ﴿and will bring you out of it﴾ also, ﴿a bringing forth﴾ on the Day of Resurrection for reckoning and recompense. ﴿And God made the earth for you a spread carpet﴾, i.e., laid out, spread flat, suitable for living upon and for life on it, ﴿that you may follow therein roads, broad paths﴾, i.e., wide ways. Thus Noah, peace be upon him, led them through the displays of God's cosmic signs, all of which indicate the existence of God, His power, knowledge, wisdom and mercy, and which necessitate worship of Him by reason, and the negation of it toward anything else. This was the problem of Noah and his account of his situation to his Lord, who knows it best. In this there is a great lesson for the guiding callers who are rightly guided, may God make us among them. Amen.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Laying out the correct path of calling, based on patience and varying the method.

2- Explanation of the disbelievers' aversion to monotheism and to the monotheists: because of their hatred of Noah and the call to monotheism, they stopped their ears so as not to hear, covered their faces so as not to see him, and grew arrogant so as not to regard him as having any merit.

3- Using wisdom in calling: when Noah saw that his people loved this world, he directed them to seeking forgiveness so that wealth and children would be obtained for them.

4- Some righteous scholars deduced from this verse that whoever has a desire for wealth or children should increase in seeking forgiveness night and day, and not tire of it, and God will grant him his wish of wealth and children.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 71, verse 21–24:

Explanation of the words:

"ʿAṣawnī" (they disobeyed me): i.e., they did not obey me in what I called them to and commanded them with, which is worshipping You alone and abandoning associating anything with You.

"Wa-ittabaʿū" (and they followed): i.e., the lowly among them and the poor.

"Man lam yazidhu māluhu wa-waladuhu" (those whom his wealth and children have not increased): i.e., the chiefs who were given blessings.

"Illā khasāran" (except in loss): i.e., in transgression and disbelief.

"Makran kibāran" (a great scheme): i.e., very great, by their denying Noah and harming him with severe harm.

"Wa-qālū" (and they said): i.e., the chiefs said to the lowly among them.

"Lā tadhunna ālihatakum" (do not abandon your gods): i.e., do not leave your gods.

"Wa-lā tadhunna" (and do not abandon): i.e., likewise do not abandon Wadd, nor Suwāʿ, nor Yaghūth, nor Yaʿūq, nor Nasr.

"Wa-qad aḍallū" (and they have led astray): i.e., by the idols, many of the people, as they commanded that they be worshipped.

Meaning of the verses:

After that noble presentation which the Messenger of God, Noah (peace be upon him), made to his Lord, asking Him to excuse and honour him, he lodged a complaint accompanied by a supplication for the destruction of the wrongdoers. "He said: My Lord, they have disobeyed me and followed one whom his wealth and children have not increased except in loss" (Qurʾān 71:21), i.e., in transgression and disbelief. "And they schemed a great scheme" (71:22), i.e., very great, in that they would mock Noah and sometimes strike him, while he remained patient and sought his reward, and they said to one another, enjoining falsehood upon each other, "Do not abandon your gods" (71:23), and they named from among them their chiefs, who were five: Wadd, Suwāʿ, Yaghūth, Yaʿūq and Nasr. "And they have led many astray" (71:24), i.e., from among the servants of God, since they inherited these idols among themselves, and the people followed them in that, and so they went astray. Then he prayed against them, saying: "And do not increase the wrongdoers except in misguidance" (71:24). He said this after he had despaired of their faith and of their guidance, because of how long he had remained among them calling them, while they increased only in disbelief and error.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The legitimacy of complaining to God Most High, but without clamour or weariness.

2- Clarification that the lowly and the poor follow the chiefs, the wealthy and the fortunate.

3- Clarification that scheming is the nature of disbelievers and wrongdoers.

4- Clarification that polytheists, in their misguidance, apply the term "gods" to the idols and images they worship.

5- The legitimacy of supplicating against wrongdoers when despairing of their guidance.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 71, verses 25–28:

Explanation of the words:

Mimma khataya'tihim ughriqu: that is, because of their sins they were drowned by the Flood.

Fa-udkhilu naran: that is, after their death their souls were made to enter the Fire.

Diyaran: that is, one who goes about, coming and going; i.e., no one was left.

In tadharhum: that is, if You leave them alive and do not destroy them.

Illa tabaran: that is, destruction and loss.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Because of their sins they were drowned﴾, informs us of the fate of the people of Nuh after Nuh had supplicated against them, having learned through divine revelation that they would not believe. Allah, may He be exalted, said: "Because of their sins," that is, "and from their sins" — meaning, because of their sins, which are polytheism, wrongdoing, denial, and harming Nuh, peace be upon him — they were drowned by the Flood, so that not one of them was left. ﴿Then they were made to enter a Fire﴾, that is, as soon as a person drowns and his soul departs, he is made to enter the Fire in the barzakh (the intermediate state). And His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿and they found for themselves, besides Allah, no helpers﴾ — and so it was; for who can help one whom Allah wills to destroy, disgrace and punish? Then He mentioned the supplication of Nuh by which the Flood and the destruction came, namely his saying: ﴿My Lord, leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dweller﴾, that is, do not leave or spare upon the dry land, on that day, any of the disbelievers, in contrast to the believers. ﴿A dweller﴾ means a person who goes about, coming and going; that is, do not spare any of the disbelievers. Then he gave the reason for his request for their destruction, saying: ﴿Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants﴾ from Your path which leads to Your pleasure, which is worshipping You alone and obeying You and Your Messenger, ﴿and they will beget none but wicked disbelievers﴾, that is, none but one who will transgress against Your religion and disbelieve in You and Your Messenger. Nuh said this because of the long trials he had endured with his people, for he had lived among them for about nine hundred and fifty years [ten centuries]. Then he supplicated Allah, may He be exalted, for himself, his parents, and whoever entered his house as a believer, and for the believing men and believing women, and that He not increase the wrongdoers except in loss and destruction, saying: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and my parents, and whoever enters my house as a believer, and the believing men and believing women, and do not increase the wrongdoers except in ruin.﴾

Lessons from the verses:

1- The destruction of the people of Nuh was because of their sins; sins are therefore a cause of destruction.

2- Affirmation of the punishment of the grave: the people of Nuh were made to enter the Fire as soon as they were drowned.

3- The legitimacy of supplicating against wrongdoers, disbelievers and criminals.

4- The legitimacy of supplicating for believing men and believing women.

5- It is recommended to begin a supplication with oneself, then extend it to those for whom one prays.
